Hugo Boss stock gets lower Citigroup target after outlook cut
sum: Citigroup lowered its price target for Hugo Boss from EUR 39.00 to EUR 38.50 on Thursday, November 5, while maintaining a Neutral rating. The move adds a fresh analyst signal after the fashion group reduced its 2026 outlook because of softer fourth-quarter demand and higher non-cash depreciation for IT assets.

AD HOC NEWS reported the analyst change on Friday, November 6. The report said the revised target reflects the weaker earnings outlook and continued uncertainty around consumer demand. Management is keeping its CLAIM 5 TOUCHDOWN strategy in place and expects further progress in gross margin and cost discipline.

Hugo Boss now expects currency-adjusted group sales to decline in the high single-digit percentage range in 2026. Its EBIT forecast is EUR 250 million to EUR 300 million, down from the previous range of EUR 300 million to EUR 350 million.

Third-quarter currency-adjusted sales fell 5 percent, while reported revenue declined 4 percent to EUR 946 million. Gross margin rose 220 basis points to 63.3 percent, but EBIT fell to EUR 81 million from EUR 95 million a year earlier. The company attributed the pressure to strategic realignment and subdued consumer demand.

The central test is whether margin expansion and tighter operating discipline can cushion weaker sales through the final quarter. Higher non-cash depreciation on selected IT and software assets adds another pressure point for reported operating profit.

Hugo Boss stock traded at EUR 38.40 on Xetra at 17:15 CET on Friday, November 6, unchanged from the Xetra close of Thursday, November 5. Real-time quote of Hugo Boss stock remains relevant as the market weighs the lower earnings range against the company's margin initiatives.
The DAX market environment remains relevant for German consumer and fashion shares.

Airtel Africa Initiates Next Share Buyback Phase with Citigroup, Targeting Up to 12 Million Shares by December 2026
sum: Airtel Africa plc (AAF), a prominent telecommunications and mobile money service provider across 14 sub-Saharan African nations, has launched the next phase of its ongoing share buyback programme. This Further Tranche, executed via Citigroup Global Markets Limited, permits the repurchase of up to 12,033,748 ordinary shares, equating to 0.33% of the company's total issued share capital as of 22 May 2026. The programme is scheduled to continue until no later than 22 December 2026, with all acquired shares set for cancellation rather than retention as treasury stock. This move aligns with Airtel Africa's capital allocation strategy focused on returning cash to shareholders.

Further Tranche Follows Completion of Initial September 2026 Buyback Phase

The buyback programme was initially announced on 22 May 2026, authorizing the repurchase of up to 1% of Airtel Africa's issued share capital at that time. After completing the Initial Tranche, disclosed on 28 September 2026, the remaining Board authority stands at 12,033,748 ordinary shares. At the annual general meeting on 9 July 2026, shareholders granted the company permission to repurchase up to 364,577,234 ordinary shares in total. Following the Initial Tranche, the residual shareholder-approved authority is 352,727,390 ordinary shares, within which the Further Tranche will operate.

sum: Bank Julius Baer & Co. Ltd Zurich reduced its Citigroup holding by 23 percent in the third quarter, according to a November 3 report by MarketBeat citing the investor's latest Securities and Exchange Commission disclosure. The fund sold 116,000 shares and retained 388,803 shares valued at 50.363 million US dollars.

The filing detail comes after Citigroup's third-quarter results, which MarketBeat says were released on October 13. Diluted earnings per share reached 2.85 US dollars, exceeding the 2.66 US dollar consensus estimate and rising from 1.86 US dollars in the year-earlier quarter. Revenue increased 7.9 percent year over year to 23.84 billion US dollars, narrowly above the 23.74 billion US dollar forecast cited in the report.

The results give investors a broader context for the ownership change. Citi delivered a quarterly earnings beat and higher revenue while continuing to return capital through its regular dividend. The earnings figures point to improved profitability compared with the same quarter last year, although the reported stake reduction reflects one institution's portfolio decision rather than a change announced by Citigroup.

Citigroup declared a quarterly dividend of 0.67 US dollars. Shareholders registered by November 2 are scheduled to receive the payment on Wednesday, November 25, according to MarketBeat. The annualized dividend is 2.68 US dollars, with the report citing a 26.15 percent payout ratio.

MarketBeat reported a consensus rating of Moderate Buy and an average analyst price target of 150.87 US dollars. The same report also listed mixed individual actions, including target reductions and ratings of Hold, underscoring that the positive consensus does not represent a uniform view.

JP Morgan Maintains "Overweight" on Korean Stocks as Citigroup Downgrades to "Neutral" After One Year
sum: Global investment banks (IBs) have recently presented mixed investment opinions regarding the sharp decline in the Korean stock market.

Employees are monitoring the stock market and exchange rates in the dealing room at the Seoul Hana Bank headquarters on the 21st, as the KOSPI successfully rebounded and closed at 6,747.95. Photo by Yonhap News

On July 21, in a report titled "Trends in the Korean Stock Market Deleveraging Process," JP Morgan stated, "While the corporate fundamentals of the Korean market remain solid, intense deleveraging (reduction of leverage) has pulled down stock prices." The KOSPI experienced a steep correction over the past month, falling approximately 28% from its recent high.

JP Morgan added, "A correction that initially began with typical concerns about fundamentals and sector rotation was amplified through leveraged ETFs, and recently, there has been a notable wave of hedge funds unwinding their positions."

The investment bank also noted that investments in artificial intelligence (AI) and data centers remain robust, maintaining its overweight view on Korean stocks and keeping its 12-month KOSPI target at 12,500.

In contrast, Citigroup downgraded its investment view on the Korean stock market from "overweight" to "neutral" for the first time in a year, according to a July 19 report. Citigroup stated, "Although corporate fundamentals in the Korean market remain favorable, recent stock price increases have heightened valuation burdens and volatility." The bank added, "From a tactical perspective, we are lowering our investment stance to neutral."

sum: Citigroup C) is proving that turnaround stories can create some of the market's best opportunities.

Following an impressive Q2 report last week that topped expectations across the board, analysts have continued raising their earnings estimates, helping Citigroup stock earn a coveted Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).
Better still, despite a remarkable rally, Citigroup stock remains the cheapest among the largest U.S. banks based on forward earnings and offers investors a respectable dividend yield.

Combined with improving profitability and a stock performance that has outperformed both JPMorgan JPM) and the broader indexes over the last three years, Citigroup appears well-positioned to extend its momentum.
Citigroup delivered one of the strongest Q2 earnings reports among the major banks.
The company generated its highest quarterly revenue in a decade at $24.76 billion, which was up 14% year over year and comfortably topped estimates of $23.67 billion by more than 4%.

More impressively, Q2 adjusted net income surged 45% to $5.8 billion from $4 billion a year ago. This translated into adjusted EPS of $3.15, crushing Wall Street expectations of $2.72 by nearly 16% and climbing more than 60% from $1.96 per share in the prior year quarter.
